[AWAITING PROPOSAL — declared mandate — 0 answer(s) on record — NO SONG YET]

REVISE ONE LINE — L2 of a 2-line draft.

You are given a draft, one line of it a grader has flagged, everything that grader
measured, and the rules it will apply to what you send back. Rewrite that ONE line.

ATTEMPT
  This is ATTEMPT 1 of this line's retry budget.
  No previous attempt was rejected on this line in this round.

THE LINE TO REVISE
  L2: Azure dog

THE WHOLE DRAFT (context — only L2 may change)
     L1  Copper cat
  >> L2  Azure dog

WHAT THE GRADER FOUND ON L2 (1)
  [flag] SCHEME_VIOLATION: L1 and L2 are both in group A [1, 2] but do not stand in the relation it requires (lines 1, 2)
      evidence: does not satisfy the declared relation 'type:rime riche' — judged by the named-type engine at that relation's own coordinate, not by the scalar comparator's admit set (score 0.737; 'cat' ~ 'dog') — NAMED PAIR IS NOT THE EVIDENCE: scored on: Copper cat  ~  Azure dog   (best of k=4)   MOSAIC (both sides): the winning span reaches back past the end word

THE RHYME MANDATE ON L2
  group A [1, 2] at its end word — this line must stand in at least one relation with: L1 ('cat') — VIOLATED, this is the word to change

OFFERED — words for the end word that answer every group bound there
  56 word(s) the band admitted are NOT offered: this place is judged by its group's declared
  relation, and it did not certify them (matt, pratt, habitat, diplomat, pussycat, democrat, copycat, format, …).
  The list below is what that relation accepts — the same judge the verdict uses.
  NOTHING OFFERED: the searched answers to 'cat' were removed by the two-tier
  ban (HOMEOTELEUTON / MODAL_RHYME; 1 under FORBIDDEN). This bounded field
  does not prove that no one-line repair exists. The GROUP (A) can move
  together through tier 2, the joint backtrack (M-105): `revise`/`finish`
  escalate there after tier 1 fails (M-205). The CLI uses `--backtrack=5`;
  connector `lyric_revise` uses `backtrack=1` by default (0 disables group
  search). Preserve every declared relation and return while rewriting.
  `capacity WORD` can also show a certified chain and the words the ban admits
  against WORD; that evidence has its own declared scope.

FORBIDDEN — do not MOVE L2 TO any of these (1)
  kat
  These are the most predictable answers in this field. MOVING to one of them is
  REJECTED OUTRIGHT — before the grader looks at whether the line fixed anything at
  all. Passing the rhyme band by reaching for the most predictable word in it is the
  slop direction, and it is the one move this loop refuses mechanically rather than
  merely discouraging (doctrine 9).

THE WORD ALREADY THERE — a DIFFERENT rule from the one above (1)
  dog
  This is the end word L2 already has. Re-proposing it is not a revision — but it
  is NOT rejected outright the way the list above is: the grader asks whether a modal
  candidate was TAKEN, and keeping the word you were given takes nothing. A line that
  keeps it is refused by rule 4 below ('nothing was fixed') UNLESS the rewrite repaired
  something else — a meter finding, say — in which case keeping it is accepted.

LINES THAT MUST NOT CHANGE
  L1 — the grader found nothing on them.
  The tool applies your one answer to L2. Every other line stays byte-identical. Changing one is rejected
  outright even if the change is an improvement.

WHAT THE GRADER ENFORCES ON YOUR ANSWER
  1. ONE line back, and it replaces L2. The draft stays 2 lines — a different
     line count is rejected outright: this loop revises lines, it does not restructure
     the draft.
  2. ONLY L2 changes (declared returns are mirrored). Any other line that comes back different is rejected
     outright, whatever else the revision achieved.
  3. The end word L2 MOVES TO is not one of the FORBIDDEN words above. That is
     checked before anything else about the line and rejects on its own. KEEPING the
     word already there is not a move and is not rejected here — see item 4.
  4. The line must FIX at least one finding. A rewrite that is differently defective
     is rejected as 'nothing was fixed'.
  5. It may not trade one defect for another: new FLAG findings anywhere in the draft
     — including on lines you did not touch — reject it once they exceed the declared
     `allow_net_new` (0 by default). New NOTES do not reject.

HOW TO ANSWER
  Send the line and nothing else: one line, no quotation marks around it, no line
  number, no commentary, no code fence. If you must explain yourself first, put the
  line LAST, alone on its own line, beginning with `LINE: `. Anything ambiguous —
  two candidate lines, a quoted line, an explanation with no marker — is discarded
  unread and costs you this attempt.
  The line is at most 200 characters; a longer one is not accepted.

CONTINUE: call lyric_revise with `run_id`, `run_revision` 1 and `answer` — the state and the draft are carried for you (run run_546765cdd2c1b87124af2e1ae3eb477c1ecf9cb8c0e25d67ddbc48a96b0273bb); `state` passed back verbatim with `answer` also works.
